title: Unified Inference — Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (May 2027)
author: Sofia Ramirez
body:
Overview

Summary
- Purpose: Present the Unified Inference product vision, high-level PRD (requirements and design), roadmap themes for the next 12 months, and pricing & packaging guidance tied to the May 2027 release.
- Audience: Product, engineering, sales, solutions, and customer success teams.

Product positioning
- One platform for consistent LLM inference across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments.
- Target customers: AI-native startups, mid-market and enterprise product teams, and platform teams needing predictable inference economics and operational controls.

Key value props
- Predictable latency & throughput across deployment modes.
- Cost controls (batching, caching, quantization recommendations).
- Unified developer experience (same API & SDKs across environments).
- Enterprise controls: KMS, audit logs, VPC, and private control plane.

High-level requirements (PRD)
1) Core use cases (MUST):
   - Low-latency text generation for product-facing endpoints (max p50 <= 80ms for 512-token model on Dedicated SLO target).
   - Scalable burst capacity for traffic spikes (support 3x baseline burst for Reserved capacity customers).
   - Cost optimization recommendations surfaced in Console (per-route suggestions for batching and quantization).

2) Developer/Integration (MUST):
   - Single REST/SDK interface for chat, completions, embeddings, and reranking.
   - Streaming responses and chunked delivery for large outputs.
   - First-class functional calls/tooling (JSON schema validation and example responses).

3) Operations & Reliability (MUST):
   - Observability: per-route latency, cost per 1k tokens, token breakdown by role, and error rates.
   - Rollouts: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to model variants.
   - SLA: 99.95% uptime for Dedicated customers (monthly SLA target).

4) Security & Compliance (SHOULD):
   - KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated, per-customer audit logging, RBAC for Console operations.

Design specification (selected items)
- API surface
  - POST /v1/generate -> body: {"model": "string", "input": "string|array", "max_tokens": "int", "stream": "bool", "call": {}}
  - POST /v1/embeddings -> body: {"model":"string","input":"string|array"}
  - All endpoints return standardized metadata: request_id, model_version, cost_estimate, timing: {queue_ms, exec_ms, network_ms}

- Runtime routing and fallbacks
  - Routing policy config (Console): primary_model, fallback_models (ordered list), latency_threshold_ms, cost_budget_per_call_usd.
  - Automatic fallback engages when exec_ms > latency_threshold_ms for 5 consecutive p50 windows or when GPU pool signals degraded capacity.

- Console UX (brief)
  - Per-route dashboard card: current model, p50/p95 latency, cost/1k tokens, percentile token distribution, recent regressions.
  - Actionable suggestions: toggle batching, apply quantization profile, pin model version, initiate canary rollout.

Non-functional requirements
- Latency targets: p50 <= 80ms (short-form gen), p95 <= 350ms (for typical request size on Dedicated SLO).
- Cost targets: 30-50% cost reduction available via recommended batching/quantization profiles for cargo workloads compared to naive per-request serving.
- Scale: platform must support a single tenant sustaining 100k concurrent requests/min across regions for large enterprise customers.

Roadmap & themes (next 12 months)
- Q2 2027 (May–Jun): May release (this doc)
   - Launch: unified API improvements (standardized timing metadata), Console cost suggestions v1, basic model fallback policies.
   - Release notes: see Release Notes section.
- Q3 2027 (Jul–Sep): Performance & cost controls
   - Intelligent batching autosuggest, multi-model KV-cache sharing, quantization profiles v2 (per-workload).
- Q4 2027 (Oct–Dec): Enterprise & Private
   - Private on-prem installer improvements, KMS/HSM integrations, audit retention configurable per-customer.
- Q1 2028 (Jan–Mar): Observability & Quality
   - Prompt-set linked regressions, built-in evals per deployment, automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Pricing & packaging notes
- Hosted API (metered): pay-as-you-go per-token for generation and per-embedding unit. Pricing tiers: Starter (low volume), Growth, Enterprise (discounted committed rate).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly commitments with burst credits. Pricing based on GPU type + guaranteed throughput.
- Private: license + support fee, optional managed updates. Additional add-ons: extended observability retention, compliance package (SOC2+ISO attestation), premium SLA.

Suggested list prices (guidance for GTM)
- Hosted generation: $0.015 / 1k tokens (Starter), $0.010 / 1k tokens (Growth), enterprise negotiated.
- Embeddings: $0.002 per vector (Starter), volume tiers for large scale.
- Dedicated: base $12k/month per GPU pool unit (example), with 30% discount on annual commit.

Packaging & bundling guidance
- Self-serve: Hosted API with Console access and basic logs, free tier credits for trial.
- Mid-market: Growth tier + dedicated account manager, monthly billing, 6–12 month commitment.
- Enterprise: Dedicated/Private options, compliance package, SSO + RBAC, extended retention, named SLAs.

Release notes (May 2027)
- Highlights
  - Unified timing metadata added to all API responses (request_id, queue_ms, exec_ms).
  - Console: Cost Suggestions v1 (per-route recommendations for batching and quantization).
  - Rollouts: model fallback policy (ordered variant list) and automatic fallback on latency violations.
  - SDK updates: streaming client improvements and function-call schema validation added.

- Migration notes for customers
  - API responses now include timing metadata; SDKs will safely ignore unknown fields but customers who compute latency should switch to the new timing fields.
  - Console cost suggestions are opt-in per-route until validated by customer.

Operational runbook (brief)
1) Pre-release checklist
   - QA: regression tests run for top 20 customer routes.
   - Perf: benchmark 50th/95th latency against Dedicated SLOs on representative models.
   - Security: confirm KMS integration pass for Private builds.
2) Post-release monitoring
   - 0–72 hours: elevated monitoring dashboard (latency, errors, cost per token).
   - Trigger page if p95 latency increases >20% for more than 30m or error rate >0.5% for 15m.
